html:
The Heiltsuk are an Indigenous people of the Central Coast of British Columbia, centred on the island village of Bella Bella. They speak a Wakashan language related to Kwak'wala.

They lived from the sea: salmon, halibut, shellfish and herring, whose roe they gathered on kelp. They built cedar plank houses and canoes and held potlatch feasts. Their neighbours include the Wuikinuxv, the Nuxalk and the Kitasoo/Xai'xais.

From the 1830s the Hudson's Bay Company traded at nearby Fort McLoughlin, and smallpox in 1862 killed many. In 1996 the Supreme Court of Canada, in a case brought by Heiltsuk herring fishers, recognised their right to sell herring spawn on kelp, an important ruling on Indigenous fishing rights. The Heiltsuk Nation governs the community today.
